titleOther: null
desc:
Five core scenarios for multi-actor work were identified and applied in the context of engagement and effective facilitation. The scenarios include:

1. Engaging and incentivising stakeholders and actors, by demonstrating the relevance and usefulness of project events/activities.
2. Interrogating existing knowledge from experts and from static sources such as EIP abstracts.
3. Creating new ideas and knowledge
a. New creative knowledge
b. Co-design of actual processes, products
4. Addressing challenges/problem solving
a. For example creating new solutions, productions, relationships, chains, networks.
5. Applying knowledge to particular contexts, scenarios: application

The identification of these scenarios is useful for the purposes of identifying methods and techniques that can be utilised for each instance. The toolbox documents participatory methods based on each scenario that can be used to be applied to any multi-actor group. The toolbox includes an interactive PDF interface. By clicking on one of the scenarios partners are brought to a Google Sheet where they can view examples of participatory tools/techniques from existing sources. These tools can be used together with stakeholders in achieving specific objectives (i.e. engaging and incensing actors and stakeholders or interrogating existing knowledge etc.). Links are provided to existing manuals and toolkits with instructions how to implement the techniques. Categories of tools/techniques to achieve each of the five objectives are allocated a unique symbol.

name: PrHo V.2.0
title: A decision support system for irrigation scheduling of greenhouse vegetable crops
titleOther: Sistema de apoyo a la toma de decisiones en la planificación del riego de cultivos hortícolas en invernadero.
desc: Software which can be used as a decision support system for irrigation scheduling in greenhouses, in relation to how much and when to irrigate, adjusted to the conditions of Almería (Spain).  It could also be adapted to other areas by previous calibration of the incorporated model. PrHo calculates the irrigation volume based on the estimation of crop evapotranspiration (ETc), which is the sum of the water lost by crop transpiration and soil evaporation. How much water to be applied is calculated from solar radiation measured outdoors and the maximum and minimum daily temperature measured inside the greenhouse. In this calculation it is possible to use average climatic data, that is available in a database that comes with the software, or real-time data if that is available. In addition, irrigation can be adapted to the particular growing conditions of each greenhouse, such as plant density, salinity of irrigation water/uniformity coefficient of the irrigation system and the transmissivity of the greenhouse cover to solar radiation (influenced by shading/whitening, greenhouse structure and cladding material).  When to irrigate can be set from user-specified criteria (interval days between irrigations or depending on the amount of water to be applied or the irrigation time) or with the help of tensiometers. The use of this tool helps the grower to optimize irrigation management and to minimize drainage losses in the soil.
descOther: Software que puede utilizarse como un sistema de apoyo a toma de decisiones en la planificación del riego en invernaderos, en relación con cuánto y cuándo regar. La aplicación esta ajustada a las condiciones de Almería (España). Puede adaptarse a otras áreas mediante la calibración previa del modelo incorporado. PrHo calcula el volumen de riego en función de la estimación de la evapotranspiración del cultivo (ETc), que es la suma del agua perdida por la transpiración del cultivo y la evaporación del suelo. La cantidad de agua que se aplicará en riego se calcula a partir de la radiación solar medida al aire libre y la temperatura diaria máxima y mínima medida dentro del invernadero. En este cálculo, es posible utilizar datos climáticos promedio, que están disponibles en una base de datos que viene con el software, o datos en tiempo real si están disponibles. En el cálculo se tienen en cuenta la densidad de plantación, la salinidad del agua de riego, el coeficiente de uniformidad del sistema de riego y la transmisividad de la cubierta del invernadero a la radiación solar (influenciada por el sombreado/encalado del invernadero) estructura y material de revestimiento). Se puede establecer cuándo regar según los criterios especificados por el usuario (días de intervalo entre riegos o según la cantidad de agua que se aplicará o el tiempo de riego) o con la ayuda de tensiómetros. El uso de esta herramienta ayuda al productor a optimizar el manejo del riego y minimizar las pérdidas de drenaje en el suelo.

name: VegSyst-DSS
title: A decision support system for the management of irrigation and nitrogen fertilization in greenhouse vegetable crops
titleOther: Un sistema de ayuda a la toma de decisión para la gestión del riego y la fertilización nitrogenada de los cultivos hortícolas bajo invernadero
desc:
VegSyst-DSS is a software developed to calculate daily N fertilizer and irrigation requirements, and the N concentration of the applied nutrient solution applied for fertigated vegetable crops grown in greenhouses. N fertilizer requirements are based on daily crop N uptake and consider soil mineral N at planting, and N mineralized from manure and soil organic matter. Irrigation requirements are based on estimated evapotranspiration (ETc) and consider irrigation application efficiency and the salinity of irrigation water.  ETc can be calculated using the Penman-Monteith equation adapted to greenhouses or the Almeria radiation equation.

VegSyst-DSS has very few inputs, all of which are readily available to farmers and advisors. Data inputs are:
- Daily maximum and minimum air temperature and relative humidity (RH) in the greenhouse, and solar radiation outside the greenhouse.
- The amount of soil mineral N in the root zone at planting.
- Details of the most recent manure application.
- Irrigation layout.
- Soil characteristics.

For the climate data, an internal database of long term average climate data for Almeria can be used; there is no requirement to enter climatic data. Recommendations based on long term average climate data are suitable for climates with very low climatic variation between years such as within greenhouses in Almeria. VegSyst DSS provides a detailed science-based plan of daily N and irrigation requirements that is specific to the characteristics of an individual crop.

VegSyst-DSS is based on the Veg-Syst crop simulation model which calculates daily crop biomass production, critical N uptake and ETc for vegetable crops. The simulation model is driven by thermal time and is adaptable to the variations in climatic conditions thereby providing N and irrigation recommendations specific to given cropping conditions such as season, time of planting, and greenhouse design and covering materials. The VegSyst-DSS assumes that crops have no water or nutrient limitations, which is almost always the case with commercial vegetable production in greenhouses.
descOther:
VegSyst-DSS es un software para calcular las necesidades diarias de nitrógeno y riego y la concentración de N a aplicar en cultivos hortícolas de invernadero fertirrigados. Las necesidades de fertilizantes de N se basan en la absorción diaria de N del cultivo y tienen en cuenta el N mineral del suelo en el momento de la plantación y el N mineralizado del estiércol y la materia orgánica del suelo. Las necesidades de riego se basan en la evapotranspiración estimada (ETc) y tienen en cuenta la eficiencia de la aplicación del riego y la salinidad del agua de riego.  La ETc puede calcularse utilizando la ecuación Penman-Monteith adaptada a los invernaderos o la ecuación de radiación de Almería.

VegSyst-DSS requiere muy pocos datos de entrada, todos los cuales están fácilmente disponibles para los agricultores y asesores. Las entradas de datos son:
- Temperatura máxima y mínima del aire y humedad relativa (HR) diaria en el invernadero, y la radiación solar fuera del invernadero.
- La cantidad de N mineral del suelo en la zona de las raíces en el momento de la plantación.
- Detalles de la aplicación más reciente de estiércol.
- Disposición de la instalación de riego.
- Características del suelo.

Para los datos climáticos, puede utilizarse una base de datos interna de datos climáticos medios a largo plazo para Almería; no es necesario introducir datos climáticos. Las recomendaciones basadas en los datos climáticos medios a largo plazo son adecuadas para climas con una variación climática muy baja entre años, como en el caso de los invernaderos de Almería. VegSyst-DSS proporciona un plan detallado basado en las necesidades diarias de N y de riego que es específico para las características de un cultivo individual.

VegSyst-DSS se basa en el modelo de simulación de cultivos de Veg-Syst, que calcula la producción diaria de biomasa de los cultivos, la absorción crítica de N y la ETc para cultivos hortícolas. El modelo de simulación opera con el tiempo térmico y es adaptable a las variaciones de las condiciones climáticas, proporcionando así recomendaciones de N y riego específicas para determinadas condiciones de cultivo, como la estación, el momento de la plantación y el diseño del invernadero y los materiales de cobertura. VegSyst-DSS asume que el cultivo no tiene limitaciones de agua o nutrientes,, lo que casi siempre ocurre en la producción comercial de hortalizas en invernaderos.

desc:
The main objective is to reduce the environmental and health risks related to the use of pesticides in plant production. One of the main activities is to produce and distribute reliable forecasts of the risks of damages by pests on agricultural crops. The data system is designed to be both a decision support system for the producer and a tool for bringing information between the consumer, the producer, the extension service and the researcher.

The risk warning is based on local information about pest development, weather prognoses from Norwegian Meteorological Institute and weather data from Nibio's weatherstations (LMT), and models that calculate risk of damages from pests and diseases. Results are presented on www.vips-landbruk.no.

This new version of VIPS is an open source technology platform for implementation of IPM tools, aimed at international collaboration and local adaptations
descOther:

titleOther: null
desc: The Soil Quality Mobile App (SQAPP) offers an easy-to-use tool that brings global soil data into the decision-making sphere of land users and other interested end users. SQAPP can, for any terrestrial location in the world for which there are soil data, provide the user with selected soil quality indicators and soil threat indicators. Rather than scoring soil quality in absolute terms, the app scores the soil quality relative to the average soil quality within areas with similar soil and climatic conditions (so-called pedo-climatic zones). For example, 80% means that only 20% of the area of the selected pedoclimatic zone is considered to have a higher indicator value than the point location being assessed. Soil threats are scored based on general, scientifically-derived threshold values. Both soil quality indicators and soil threat indicators with low scores are indicated and management solutions are suggested for the combination of indicators flagged as low in a specific location.

name: IKMIS
title: A system of integrated plant protection information, consulting and training
titleOther: Integruotos augalų apsaugos informavimo, konsultavimo ir mokymų informacinė sistema
desc: IKMIS is a system of integrated plant protection information, consulting, and training, consisting of 4 free electronic services for farmers, advisers, researchers, and anyone interested in agriculture. The aim of the system is to inform the Lithuanian agricultural sector about the occurrence of harmful organisms in crops, to improve their skills and to speed up optimal decisions on the use of plant protection products, thus reducing the negative impact on the environment, human and animal health in Lithuania.  The system promotes both a sparing use of plant protection products and a use of non-chemical integrated pest management techniques. Data from insect traps, online weather stations and weather forecasts are integrated and automatically fed into the system. The data is used to recommend when not to spray fields, up-to-date information on the spread of harmful organisms in different crops in all regions of Lithuania is provided, as well as timely interactive advice. During the growing season, farmers' crops are monitored, plant surveys are carried out according to a methodology developed by scientists, and data and recommendations are provided by the plant production advisers of the Advisory Service. To ensure the quality of the advice, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), satellite data and nitrogen demand measurement devices are used to determine the health status of crops. If you observe your crop and suspect a disease or pest is spreading, but are unable to identify the pest or disease, you can find all the information you need in the system. The catalogues of diseases, pests and weeds are published in IKMIS to help identify the disease or pest more quickly and to make it easier to choose the plant protection products registered in Lithuania to control them. The catalogues are continuously updated by researchers at the Lithuanian Research Centre for Agriculture and Forestry, and the information in the plant protection product database is directly delivered from the database of the State Plant Production Service. Farms using plant protection products must comply with the requirements of Integrated Pest Management. By filling in a questionnaire in the system, each user can find out whether the farm complies with these requirements and, if not, is given information on areas for improvement. If advice is needed on the application of integrated pest management practices, an adviser can be contacted via the IKMIS system. Another important service of IKMIS is training. Farmers have to continuously improve their qualifications and knowledge through various courses, trainings, and seminars, which are not always organised in the area where they live, thus they have to travel to other towns. With the IKMIS distance learning service – which consists of more than 15 training programmes – farmers will be able to learn at home, in a way and at a time that suits them best. This way they can save their valuable time and money. Most importantly, almost all IKMIS services (except distance learning) are free of charge and available to anyone with internet access.

Pagal gaunamus duomenis rekomenduojama, kada nereikėtų purkšti laukų, pateikiama operatyvi informacija apie kenksmingų organizmų plitimą įvairių žemės ūkio augalų pasėliuose visuose Lietuvos rajonuose, ir teikiamos savalaikės interaktyvios konsultacijos. Vegetacijos metu ūkininkų pasėlius stebi, augalų apskaitas pagal mokslininkų parengtą metodiką atlieka ir duomenis bei rekomendacijas teikia Konsultavimo tarnybos augalininkystės konsultantai. Stebint savo pasėlius ir įtarus, kad jame plinta liga ar kenkėjas, bet nesugebant identifikuoti kenkėjo ar ligos – vartotojas sistemoje gali rasti visą jam aktualią informaciją. IKMIS skelbiami ligų, kenkėjų ir piktžolių katalogai, padedantys greičiau atpažinti ligą ar kenkėją ir lengviau pasirinkti juos naikinančius Lietuvoje registruotus augalų apsaugos produktus. Katalogus nuolat atnaujina Lietuvos agrarinių ir miškų mokslų centro mokslininkai, o į augalų apsaugos produktų duomenų bazę informacija gaunama tiesiai iš Valstybinės augalininkystės tarnybos duomenų bazės. Sistemoje užpildęs anketą, kiekvienas vartotojas sužino, ar ūkis juos atitinka, jeigu neatitinka – pateikiama informacija apie tobulintinas ūkio veiklos sritis. name: Teagasc AgileTECH Advisory Facilitation Method
title: Facilitation Method: Managing Grass
titleOther: null
desc: The AgileTECH project aimed to understand the relevance and use of existing scientific knowledge regarding grassland management among farmers. In this context, the project co-designed a method for use by advisers in a discussion group context. Sheep, beef and dairy farmers and farm advisers were involved in five focus groups, which were recorded, transcribed and analysed. The analysis informed subsequent co-design stages, involving scientists, specialists, farm advisers and graphic designers. A group facilitation method to encourage farmer engagement with grassland management was co-designed and prototyped by the group. The method reflects findings from across the focus groups conducted with farmers and advisers and contains four main elements: building farmer-adviser rapport and approaching ‘goal setting’ with clients, which was identified as a crucial first step; building ‘Managing Grass Action Plans’, which takes a flexible approach to supporting farmers to identify cost-effective, impactful and achievable actions on their farms; use of storyboards (illustrated stories) to facilitate the group to address social (relationship), cultural (pride) and economic issues associated with managing grass; and, finally, a discussion group self-evaluation method (‘health check’) to improve group functioning (organisation, trust, solidarity, learning, fun and enjoyment). The group facilitation method is presented in print and interactive PDF form, accompanied by a customised carry bag containing the co-designed resource materials required to implement the extension method. Over 20 farm advisers (Teagasc and the cooperative sector) have received training to use the method and are currently practising it and generating feedback on its use.
keywords: advisory, facilitation, grassland management
creator: 5e186b019b113a708c7e1b5e

desc: Sociological factors (i.e., farmers’ routines, practices, beliefs and values) regarding animal health have implications for disease management, specifically implementation of critical control points (CCPs, following HACCP) to control Johne’s disease at farm level. The research findings were channelled into a transdisciplinary co-design process, involving the interrogation of the findings by groups of farmers, veterinary practitioners, veterinary scientists, policy-makers, farm advisers, and cooperative representatives. In a sequence of workshops, the multi-actor groups co-designed a suite of practical actions to implement the CCPs at farm level. The process evolved to include an artist and graphic designer, who worked with the multi-actor team to translate the practical implementation actions into interactive and visual tools. In addition to recording templates (e.g., hygiene, calving etc., necessary for implementing the HACCP approach), information briefs and storyboards (illustrated stories) were co-designed. Based directly on farmers’ and other actors’ stories, storyboards have diverse purposes. They present ‘how to’ information graphically, while also incorporating in vernacular language the social (relationship), cultural (pride) and economic (monetary) factors that arise in decision making. Veterinarians and advisers can use storyboards to prompt discussion with farmers of contentious or sensitive issues, deflecting the focus onto a hypothetical case rather than focusing on the farmers personally. Storyboards were developed to show the negotiation of particular beliefs/values held by farmers in relation to disease control, necessary for practical implementation of the CCPs. Together with information briefs and CCP recording templates, the storyboards are presented in a comprehensive printed document, and in an interactive PDF for use on touchscreen and conventional devices such as tablets, androids and computers.
keywords: Advisors, facilitation, disease, cattle, Johne's disease

name: Forest Investment Valuation Estimator (FIVE)
title: Forestry Investment Valuation Support Tool
titleOther: null
desc:
The Teagasc Forest Investment Valuation Estimator (FIVE) as a decision-support
tool, using Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) analysis to model indicative financial returns for
forestry land-use options in Ireland. The MS Excel Model provides indicative analysis and decision
support, particularly in relation to reviewing pre-planting options and comparing criteria
such as species, yield classes and rotation lengths according to landowners’ preferences and
objectives.
Potential timber revenues are generated by the FIVE tool through the selection of stand
characteristics and management regimes. A range of variables are used as inputs in a typical
analysis, including species, site productivity, rotation length, relevant premium payments,
establishment and on-going management costs, thinning and clearfell timber volumes and
revenues potentially attainable. The FIVE tool has been used in previous studies of forestry
and agricultural incomes (e.g. Ryan et al., 2014, 2016).
Future cost and revenue streams from forestry are generated in FIVE which are then
discounted to present day values and presented as net present values.
The FIVE tool requires regular updating to ensure input data (e.g. Government forest premium payments) and timber prices are appropriate.

2.	Economy,

This saves time for advisers and farmers and reduces the likelihood of errors. Having farm data in one place not only allows a quick and objective assessment of a real farm situation, but also identification of the main problems, taking of appropriate actions and planning a long-term perspective for the farm.

name: OPTIPROTECT
title: Optiprotect is an easy-to-use and reliable Decision Support Tool (DST) that allows you to better defend your wheat crops.
titleOther: Optiprotect est un Outil d’aide à la décision (OAD) simple d’utilisation et fiable qui vous permet de mieux défendre vos cultures de blé.
desc:
With Optiprotect, protect your wheat crops from diseases and avoid crop losses
Optiprotect is an easy-to-use and reliable Decision Support Tool (DST) that allows you to better defend your wheat crops. Thanks to a precise monitoring of the growth stages of your crops and the risks of fungal diseases, you use the right doses of phytosanitary products, in the right place and at the right time, for a more sustainable agriculture.
Optiprotect values your operating data from MesParcelles whether you are a subscriber or not. If you are not subscribed to MesParcelles, an advisory right is created for an exclusive use of the tool. The uploading of your data is done automatically without the need to re-enter it.
How does the tool work?
Your customized parcel data from MesParcelles are cross-referenced with the spatialized climatological data from Météo France station network. Arvalis-Institut du Végétal's algorithmic models thus predict the dates on which the growth stages of your crops will be reached (ear 1 cm, 1 node, 2 nodes, Last spread leaf - DFE, heading, flowering) and the optimal dates for observation and phytosanitary treatment against the main wheat pests (Downy Mildew, Septoria, Yellow Rust, Brown Rust and Fusarium).
The Optiprotect interface, accessible from your tablet or computer, takes the form of a simple and effective dashboard. Thanks to a specific color code, it allows you to quickly read the evolution of stages and disease risks for all your wheat plots.
You have the possibility to adjust your local weather data in case of very localised bad weather.
Your crops are defended and your interventions secured.
Thanks to Optiprotect you receive:
- Weekly newsletters by e-mail concerning the sanitary state of each of your plots of land.
- Customized notifications on your dashboard
- SMS alerts in advance of key dates for phytosanitary treatments.

By telephone or in the field, your adviser is at your disposal throughout the campaign, to inform you about local illnesses, the correct dosages to be carried out or the adaptation of the treatment day.

Finally for an integrated protection of your crops year after year, Optiprotect offers you the possibility to make a global and technical analysis at the end of your campaigns and to automatically save the history to compare several campaigns.
descOther:
Avec Optiprotect, protégez vos cultures de blé des maladies et évitez les pertes de récolte
Optiprotect est un Outil d’aide à la décision simple d’utilisation et fiable qui vous permet de mieux défendre vos cultures de blé. Grâce à un suivi précis des stades de croissance de vos cultures et des risques de maladies fongiques, vous utilisez les bonnes doses de produits phytosanitaires, au bon endroit et au bon moment, pour une agriculture plus durable.
Optiprotect valorise les données de votre exploitation issues de MesParcelles que vous soyez abonné et non abonné. Si vous n’êtes pas abonné à MesParcelles, un droit consultatif est créé pour une utilisation exclusive de l’outil. La remontée de vos données se fait automatiquement sans contrainte de ressaisie.
Comment fonctionne l'outil ? 
Vos données parcellaires personnalisées issues de MesParcelles sont croisées aux données climatologiques spatialisées issues du réseau de stations Météo France. Les modèles algorithmiques d’Arvalis-Institut du Végétal prédisent ainsi les dates d’atteinte des stades de croissance de vos cultures (épi 1 cm, 1 nœud, 2 nœuds, Dernière Feuille étalée - DFE, épiaison, floraison) et les dates optimales d’observation et de traitement phytosanitaire contre les principaux bioagresseurs du blé (Piétin verse, Septoriose, Rouille jaune, Rouille brune et Fusariose).
L’interface Optiprotect, accessible depuis votre tablette ou ordinateur, se présente sous forme d’un tableau de bord simple et efficace. Grâce à un code couleur spécifique, elle vous permet une lecture rapide de l’évolution des stades et des risques de maladies pour toutes vos parcelles de blés.
Vous avez la possibilité d’ajuster vos données météorologiques locales dans le cas d’intempéries très localisées.
Vos cultures sont défendues et vos interventions sécurisées 
Grâce à Optiprotect vous recevez :
•	Des lettres d’information hebdomadaires par mail concernant l’état sanitaire de chacune de vos parcelles
•	Des notifications personnalisées sur votre tableau de bord
•	Des alertes SMS en amont des dates clés de traitement phytosanitaire.
Par téléphone ou sur le terrain, votre conseiller est à votre disposition tout au long de la campagne.
Enfin pour une protection intégrée de vos cultures année après année, Optiprotect vous offre la possibilité de faire une analyse globale et technique à l’issue de vos campagnes et de sauvegarder automatiquement l’historique pour comparer plusieurs campagnes.

name: Slaughter weight optimisation - Slachtdoordacht
title: This is a calculation tool that gives  an insight into the most important mechanisms to optimise slaughter weight
titleOther: Slachtdoordacht, tool voor varkenshouders om management beslissingen met betrekking tot het optimaal afleveren van vleesvarkens te evalueren
desc:
The tool allows the user to gain insight into the optimal slaughter weight for the fattening pigs and the economic importance of the optimisation. The model calculates the changes in the gross balance per fattening pig delivered and per pig place per year as a function of increasing fattening time and increasing weight of the pig. The optimisation model then looks for the fattening duration with the highest gross balance per pig place per year. 

In addition, the tool also lends itself very well to analysing the effect on the gross balance of improvements in the pigs' key figures or of changes in the  market conditions. The design of the learning module is that users can learn by performing various simulations and by using different parameter values to gain insight into the effect of these changes. 

The tool has a configuration page, where the parameters for slaughter yield, manure production and weight categories, linked with its discounts and surcharges from the slaughterhouse, can be adapted for each farms' situation. On the simulation page of the tool, you can make a simulation for the set with your own parameters, adapting the animal technical data, the economic data and the simulation features (number of production rounds). The results of these simulations can be found on the result page of the tool, showing several graphs and tabels, describing optimisation,  evolutions in turnover and costs, and the animal-technical performances.
descOther:
Zoals de naam doet vermoeden willen de makers van de tool de Vlaamse varkenshouders ondersteunen in het maken van de juiste beslissingen omtrent het slachtgewicht van hun vleesvarkens. De tool laat de gebruiker toe om inzicht te verkrijgen in het optimale slachtgewicht voor de vleesvarkens en het economische belang van de optimalisatie. 
Daarnaast leent de tool zich ook prima tot het analyseren van het effect op het bruto saldo van verbeteringen in de kengetallen bij de vleesvarkens of van wijzigende marktomstandigheden. Het opzet van de leermodule is dat de gebruikers kunnen bijleren door
verschillende simulaties uit te voeren en door te spelen met verschillende parameterwaarden tot inzicht komen in het effect van deze wijzigingen.

desc:
Optimize your nitrogen fertilization thanks to satellite and drone images
Do you wish to better control the fertility of your soils through precision farming? Optimize your nitrogen fertilization on wheat, barley and rapeseed? Our decision support tool (OAD Fertilization) accessible from MesParcelles service platform has been developed to allow you to make the right decision at the right time and in the right place.
How does the tool work?
Using satellite or drone imagery, you can obtain a map of the biomass of your plots in order to follow the evolution of the state of your crops.
The resulting recommendation map informs you about the yield potential of your crops and the right amount of nitrogen fertilizer to use, taking into account the heterogeneity of your plots. You can thus adjust the nitrogen fertilization during the season in relation to the planned balance sheet dose to achieve your yield and quality objectives.
Precise and tailor-made maps!
- The maps are accessible in digital version from your smartphone or tablet and can be valorized in MesParcelles in the fertilization management module.
- The modulation cards provided as part of the service can be inserted on your console and will allow you to modulate your nitrogenous fertilization to the nearest square meter.
- The console provides you with an application map allowing you to compare actual and forecast interventions.
- Throughout the process, an advisor from the Chamber of Agriculture will provide you with agronomic expertise to help you interpret the maps in order to best adjust your fertilizer intake to the situation.
- A hotline is available and an advisor can visit your farm by appointment.
- The imaging models used are tested and certified by our network of agricultural experts at the Chambers of Agriculture.
Data acquisition chain with the OAD Fertilization of MesParcelles
1- Ordering the online service from the platform MesParcelles. For the plots to be analyzed, acquisition of satellite imagery or processing drone. 
2- Automatic registration of the recommendation map in the Fertilization module of MesParcelles. 
3- Interpretation and possibility of adjustment of the data by the farmer (autonomous action or accompanied by your adviser). 
4- Transfer of the modulation card in your console for an automatic modulation of the field interventions. 
5- Application map of the actual interventions compared to the forecast.

name: Agriorisk
title: Forecast model for wireworm damage
titleOther: Voorspellingsmodel ritnaaldenschade
desc:
A prediction model for the presence of damage caused by wireworms was developed based on the harmful wireworm species collected and their numbers over the last four years, in combination with the soil parameters and the cultivation history of the plots monitored. The 'random forest' machine learning model proved to be the most reliable and transparent method. Based on the data of 235 plots, ten factors seem to determine the presence of harmful wireworm species. The important parcel parameters are soil type, acidity (pH) and organic matter content. For the plot history, the main crops and the number of years of cereals/grass/maize as the main crop over the past five years seem important. The presence of a green cover in the winter prior to cultivation and the type of tillage carried out one to four years ago may in certain circumstances also have an impact on the occurrence of wireworms.  
Most of the plot parameters and the history of each plot are available through the VLM database (in Flanders) and have been converted into usable map layers for the platform. Any missing model parameters for the intended plot are requested from the user. Linking the predicted wireworm pressure to the main crop of the new season allows the underlying model to calculate the risk of crop damage. The web platform displays a colour code per field, which makes the risk of wireworm damage clear to the grower. An advice is linked to this colour code about the possible measures the grower can take. Among other things, the grower is advised to carry out a sampling on the risk plot. For this purpose, reference is made to the protocol for placing traps.
descOther:
Op basis van de verzamelde schadelijke ritnaaldsoorten en hun aantallen gedurende de afgelopen vier jaar, in combinatie met de bodemparameters en teeltgeschiedenis van de gemonitorde percelen, werd een voorspellingsmodel voor de aanwezigheid van schade door ritnaalden ontwikkeld. Het ‘machine-learning’ model ‘random forest’  bleek de meest betrouwbare en transparante methode. Gebaseerd op de gegevens van 235 percelen lijkt een tiental factoren bepalend te zijn voor de aanwezigheid van schadelijke ritnaaldsoorten. De belangrijke perceelsparameters zijn het bodemtype, de zuurtegraad (pH) en het organisch stofgehalte. Voor de perceelshistoriek lijken de hoofdteelten en het aantal jaren granen/gras/mais als hoofdteelt in de afgelopen vijf jaar belangrijk. De aanwezigheid van een groenbedekker in de winter voorafgaand aan de teelt en het type grondbewerking (kerend of niet-kerend) die één tot vier jaar geleden werden uitgevoerd, kunnen in bepaalde omstandigheden ook een impact hebben op het voorkomen van ritnaalden.
De meeste perceelsparameters en de historiek van elk perceel zijn beschikbaar via de VLM-databank en werden omgezet in bruikbare kaartlagen voor het platform. Eventueel ontbrekende modelparameters voor het beoogde perceel worden opgevraagd aan de gebruiker. Het koppelen van de voorspelde ritnaalddruk aan de hoofdteelt van het nieuwe seizoen laat het achterliggende model toe het risico op gewasschade te berekenen. Het webplatform geeft per perceel een kleurcode weer, welke het risico op ritnaaldenschade duidelijk maakt voor de teler. Aan deze kleurcode wordt een advies gekoppeld over de mogelijke maatregelen die de teler kan nemen. De teler wordt onder andere aangeraden een bemonstering op het risicoperceel uit te voeren. Hiervoor wordt verwezen naar het protocol om lokvallen te plaatsen.
keywords: wireworm, risk calculation, crop damage, advice

name: IMAGO
title: Toolbox for region-specific rural development
titleOther: Toolbox voor gebiedsgerichte plattelandsontwikkeling
desc:
IMAGO stands for Integrated Method for Action-oriented Regional Development. The toolbox - a set of methods and tools - can be used by coordinators of region-specific rural development processes to improve the process they are involved with. The focus is on rural development processes related to the management of open space. How do you get an overview of all projects in open space in a certain area? How can these projects be better coordinated with each other? How can rural actors work together?

IMAGO offers five tools for regio-specific rural development. 

EXPLORE: "The EXPLORE tool helps users to get a good picture of their working area, both spatially and socio-economically. The tool provides four tools (actor analysis, project inventory, aerial photographs and maps) to get to know the actors, projects, developments, opportunities and threats of open space in your area".
DEBATE: "This tool opens up the debate on open space with municipal officials and politicians. It makes users think about open space and the policies they pursue. The tool is based on three debating sessions and provides tools to process the results of those sessions".
PLAY: "Visionary is a method to interactively discuss the opportunities and threats to open space in a region. The PLAY tool offers two versions of Visionary: a general version for awareness raising and a customised version for vision development. Visionary is based on the serious game Participology of Birmingham City University".
COMBINE: "The COMBINE tool provides a handy overview of all open space instruments in Flanders. The atlas is not exhaustive, but very comprehensive. It also offers support to use or combine instruments".
EVALUATE: "This tool helps you reflect on region-specific actions in open space. What is the impact on an area? Are actors missing? The tool is divided into a meta-evaluation, which you carry out before the start of a new project, and an evaluation of an ongoing initiative".
descOther:
IMAGO staat voor Geïntegreerde Methode voor Actiegerichte GebiedsOntwikkeling. Het doel is om een toolbox te ontwikkelen - een set van methoden en instrumenten - die gebruikt kan worden door coördinatoren van gebiedsgerichte plattelandsontwikkelingsprocessen om het proces waar zij bij betrokken zijn te verbeteren. Hoe krijg je een overzicht van alle projecten in de open ruimte in een bepaald gebied? Hoe kunnen die projecten beter op elkaar worden afgestemd? Op welke manier kunnen plattelandsactoren samenwerken? 
IMAGO biedt vijf tools voor gebiedsgerichte ontwikkeling. 

VERKEN: “De VERKEN-tool helpt gebruikers om een goed beeld te krijgen van hun werkingsgebied, zowel op ruimtelijk als op socio-economisch vlak. De tool reikt vier hulmiddelen aan (actoranalyse, projectinventaris, luchtfoto’s en kaarten) om de actoren, projecten, ontwikkelingen, kansen en bedreigingen van open ruimte in je gebied te leren kennen.”
DEBATTEER: “Deze tool opent het debat over open ruimte met ambtenaren en politici van gemeentebesturen. Hij doet gebruikers nadenken over open ruimte en het beleid dat ze voeren. De tool gaat uit van drie debatteersessies en reikt handvaten aan om de resultaten van die sessies te verwerken.”
SPEEL: “Visionary is een methode om op een interactieve manier de kansen en bedreigingen voor de open ruimte in een streek te bespreken. De SPEEL-tool biedt twee versies van Visionary aan: een algemene versie voor sensibilisering en een versie op maat voor visieontwikkeling. Visionary is gebaseerd op de serious game Participology van Birmingham City University.”
COMBINEER: “De COMBINEER-tool biedt een handig overzicht van alle openruimte-instrumenten in Vlaanderen. De atlas is niet exhaustief, maar wel heel uitgebreid. Hij biedt ook ondersteuning om instrumenten te gebruiken of te combineren.”
EVALUEER: “Deze tool helpt je bij het reflecteren over gebiedsgerichte acties in de open ruimte. Wat is de impact op een gebied? Ontbreken er actoren? De tool is verdeeld in een meta-evaluatie, die je uitvoert voor de start van een nieuw project, en een evaluatie van een lopend initiatief.”
keywords: regio-specific, rural development, toolbox, coordination, open space, debate, evaluate

title: Spraytech web tool for better choices in spray technique and less diffuse pollution when using pesticides

desc:
The tool helps to immediately make the right decisions about spray nozzles, pressure, buffer zones, product, etc. – all in function of the crop and the problem (pests or disease). For farmers/horticulturists and professional users of pesticides, the tool provides practical help to spray more efficiently, with less overrun, and less environmental pressure. The tool is based on a series of large background databases full of information such as the characteristics of each existing commercial spray nozzle and every pesticide approved for use.
 It helps farmers to make the right choices in terms of:
- Spray technology to be used (type of sprayer, nozzle size and type, pressure, speed of driving) 
- Product to be used
- Buffer zone required along a waterway
The three factors – three circles in the web tool, fuelled by databases – are all coupled to each other.

In the circles 'Spraying technique' and 'Product' , the user can go through various scenarios step-by-step via dropdowns. The 'Buffer zone' sphere always indicates the width of the buffer zone along a watercourse to be respected based on the chosen product and in combination with the chosen spraying technique.
descOther:
De interactieve webtool is ontwikkeld om in één oogopslag de juiste beslissing te treffen over spuitdoppen, druk, bufferzone, product, … telkens naargelang de (vollegronds) teelt en het probleem (plaag of ziekte). Voor landbouwers en professionele gebruikers van gewasbeschermingsmiddelen wordt de tool naar verwachting een nuttige hulp om efficiënter te spuiten, met minder overbodig verlies en minder belasting voor het milieu. De tool draait op een reeks omvangrijke achterliggende databases, bijvoorbeeld over de kenmerken van elke bestaande commerciële spuitdop en elk erkend gewasbeschermingsmiddel.

Ze helpt landbouwers om in functie van de te bestrijden plaag correcte keuzes te maken op het vlak van:
- Te gebruiken spuittechniek (type spuittoestel, doptype en -grootte, druk, rijsnelheid)
- Toe te passen gewasbeschermingsmiddel of product
- Te respecteren breedte van spuitvrije bufferzone langs een waterloop
De drie factoren – drie bollen in de webtool, telkens gevoed met databases - zijn onlosmakelijk met elkaar verbonden. 

Op dit moment is de tool operationeel voor alle volleveldstoepassingen, dus akkerbouw en groenten.
In de bollen ‘Spuittechniek’ en de ‘Product’ kan de gebruiker verschillende scenario’s stapsgewijs doorlopen via dropdowns. De ‘Bufferzone’ bol geeft telkens de te respecteren breedte van de bufferzone langs een waterloop aan op basis van het gekozen product en in combinatie met de gekozen spuittechniek.

name: WELLTRANS
title: animal-friendly chicken transport
titleOther: Diervriendelijk kippentransport
desc:
Reserachers of Ghent University and ILVO established a protocol to evaluate the welfare of broiler chickens during the pre-slaughter phase. The protocol includes nine welfare indicators that include how severely the animals have suffered from heat or cold stress, constriction of wings, toes or heads, and so on. The evaluation of all indicators results in a general welfare index. 

Transport to the slaughterhouse can be a very unpleasant experience for broiler chickens. In order to improve welfare during that journey, researchers from UGent and ILVO developed an evaluation protocol that uses a welfare index to indicate how much or little the animals have suffered. From two experiments, an observational study, an inventory of the current transport situation and interviews with people from the sector, a practical protocol was developed that can be used in the slaughterhouse.

A total of nine welfare indicators were defined, all of which can be evaluated at the slaughterhouse by a trained person. The first part is a welfare evaluation at the end of the waiting period at the slaughterhouse, which looks at the occurrence of heat or cold stress, constrictions (wings, toes, heads), chickens with spreader legs, displacement (one chicken on top of another) and so-called back girders. The aim is to observe approximately sixty crates or drawers per hen.

Then the prevalence of fractures and bruises on the slaughter line will be determined. For each slaughter line indicator the target is to observe 10 minutes. The implementation of the complete protocol takes about 60 minutes per tome transported. After the evaluation of all indicators, it is intended that the quotations are merged into a score that serves as a general welfare index. For this purpose,

"This welfare index makes it possible to identify specific animal welfare bottlenecks. In addition, the welfare index makes it possible to compare different transports, but also different slaughterhouses, catching teams, poultry farmers, and so on. The score can serve as a guide to implement and evaluate welfare improvements, and can possibly even be used as the basis for an animal welfare label in which only meat that meets a certain score can be sold".
descOther:
Onderzoekers van UGent en het Instituut voor Landbouw- en Visserij- en Voedingsonderzoek (ILVO) hebben een protocol opgesteld om het welzijn van vleeskippen tijdens de pre-slachtfase te evalueren. Het protocol omvat negen welzijnsindicatoren die onder meer nagaan hoe sterk de dieren hebben geleden onder hitte- of koudestress, beklemmingen van vleugels, tenen of koppen, enzovoort. De evaluatie van alle indicatoren resulteert in een algemene welzijnsindex. 

Het transport naar het slachthuis kan voor vleeskippen een erg onaangename ervaring zijn. Om het welzijn tijdens die rit te verbeteren, werkten onderzoekers van UGent en ILVO een evaluatieprotocol uit dat via een welzijnsindex aangeeft hoeveel of weinig de dieren te lijden hebben gehad. Vanuit twee experimenten, een observationele studie, een inventaris van de huidige transportsituatie en interviews met mensen uit de sector werd een praktisch protocol uitgewerkt dat in het slachthuis gebruikt kan worden.

In totaal werden negen welzijnsindicatoren gedefinieerd die allemaal op het slachthuis geëvalueerd kunnen worden door een getraind persoon. Het eerste onderdeel is een welzijnsevaluatie aan het eind van de wachtperiode op het slachthuis waarbij wordt gekeken naar het optreden van hitte- of koudestress, beklemmingen (vleugels, tenen, koppen), kippen met spreidpoten, verdringing (een kip bovenop een andere) en zogenaamde rugliggers. Per toom wordt beoogd om ongeveer zestig kratten of lades te observeren.

Daarna worden de prevalentie van breuken en bloeduitstortingen aan de slachtlijn bepaald. Per slachtlijnindicator is het streefdoel om 10 minuten te observeren. De uitvoering van het volledige protocol duurt ongeveer 60 minuten per getransporteerde toom. Na het evalueren van alle indicatoren is het de bedoeling dat de quoteringen samengevoegd worden tot een score die fungeert als een algemene welzijnsindex. 

“Deze welzijnsindex laat toe om specifieke knelpunten voor dierenwelzijn te identificeren. Daarnaast maakt de welzijnsindex het mogelijk om verschillende transporten, maar ook verschillende slachthuizen, vangploegen, pluimveehouders, enzovoort, te vergelijken. De score kan dienen als leidraad om welzijnsverbeteringen door te voeren en te evalueren, en kan mogelijk zelfs als basis gebruikt worden voor een dierenwelzijnskeurmerk waarbij enkel vlees verkocht kan worden dat aan een bepaalde score voldoet.”

name: ILVO Farmer Entrepreneur Scan – ILVO Ondernemersscan voor Landbouwers
title: ILVO Farmers Entrepreneur Scan
titleOther: ILVO Ondernemersscan voor Landbouwers
desc:
To respond to the challenges of sustainable agricultural development it is no longer sufficient for farmers and growers to be a craftsman. Entrepreneurial and management skills are becoming increasingly important. Farmers and growers are thus forced to learn and further professionalize in the field of entrepreneurship. 
A Farmer Entrepreneur Scan was developed to support entrepreneurship in agriculture and horticulture. Intended users are extension workers and study clubs in agriculture and horticulture, where it can be used to guide companies toward sustainable entrepreneurship. In addition to the use as a stand-alone instrument, the scan can be integrated in tools for integrated sustainability assessment. 

The ILVO Farmer Entrepreneur Scan is hierarchically structured according to 8 themes, which are further subdivided into 15 indicators. The 8 themes are:  Vision-Strategy, Planning-Organization-Control, Networking-Collaboration, Risk Management, Opportunity Recognition and Exploitation, Searching and Learning Behavior, Innovation and Craftsmanship. These themes and indicators are visually presented in a radar plot (see figure). The radar plot gives a clear overview of the position of a farm on the level of the entrepreneurial themes and indicators. All scores are shown on a scale of 0 to 100. The width of a segment determines the relative importance of a theme or indicator. A bold black line indicates the mean of a reference group of companies.
descOther:
Om een antwoord te bieden op de uitdagingen van duurzame landbouwontwikkeling is het niet langer voldoende dat boeren en telers een ambachtsman zijn. Ondernemerschap en managementvaardigheden worden steeds belangrijker. Boeren en telers worden dus gedwongen om te leren en zich verder te professionaliseren op het gebied van ondernemerschap. 
Om het ondernemerschap in de land- en tuinbouw te ondersteunen is een Ondernemersscan ontwikkeld. Bedoelde gebruikers zijn voorlichters en studieclubs in de land- en tuinbouw, waar het gebruikt kan worden om bedrijven te begeleiden naar duurzaam ondernemen. Naast het gebruik als een op zichzelf staand instrument kan de scan worden geïntegreerd in tools voor integrale duurzaamheidsbeoordeling. 

De Ondernemersscan is hiërarchisch gestructureerd volgens 8 thema's, die verder zijn onderverdeeld in 15 indicatoren. De 8 thema's zijn:  Visie-Strategie, Planning-Organisatie-Controle, Netwerk-Samenwerking, Risicomanagement, Kanserkenning en -exploitatie, Zoek- en Leergedrag, Innovatie en Vakmanschap. Deze thema's en indicatoren worden visueel gepresenteerd in een radarplot (zie figuur). Het radarplot geeft een duidelijk overzicht van de positie van een bedrijf op het niveau van de ondernemersthema's en indicatoren. Alle scores worden weergegeven op een schaal van 0 tot 100. De breedte van een segment bepaalt het relatieve belang van een thema of indicator. Een vetgedrukte zwarte lijn geeft het gemiddelde van een referentiegroep van bedrijven aan.

name: Animal Welfare scan - Dierenwelzijnsscan
title: Determine the level of animal welfare on the company
titleOther: Bepalen van het dierenwelzijn op het bedrijf
desc:
There is a self-scan per animal species (cattle, pigs, poultry) and per industry (for cattle: dairy cattle and beef cattle).

Good animal welfare is achieved by complying with the 'five freedoms'. The welfare app contains indicators for each of these freedoms:

Free from hunger & thirst
Free of inconvenience
Free from pain, injury & illness
Free to show normal behavior
Free from anxiety and chronic stress.

The first part of the scan (tile GENERAL) can be completed by the cattle farmer at his desk. This involves questions about housing, breed and various key figures.

In addition, there are the scans for the barn itself. 

After completing the questionnaire, the farmer will automatically receive a report by e-mail. This also contains the welfare radar (see figure). It shows various welfare indicators on a scale from 0% (very poor) to 100% (very good). The farmer also receives more information online about possible risk factors (www.dierenwelzijnscan.be). He can then discuss with the farm veterinarian which measures may be applied to improve animal welfare.

If the scan is taken at regular intervals (e.g. twice a year), the evolution of the animal welfare level on the farm can also be monitored. The effect of management changes on animal welfare can also be investigated.

In addition, if there is sufficient participation, members of The Farmers Union of Flanders can compare their scores with those of fellow farmers. Of course, this is completely anonymous.
descOther:
Er is een zelfscan per diersoort (rundvee, varkens, pluimvee) en per bedrijfstak (voor rundvee: melkvee en vleesvee). 

Een goed dierenwelzijn wordt bekomen door te voldoen aan de ‘vijf vrijheden’. De welzijnsapp bevat indicatoren voor elk van deze vrijheden:

Vrij van honger & dorst
Vrij van ongemak
Vrij van pijn, verwondingen & ziekte
Vrij om normaal gedrag te vertonen
Vrij van angst en chronische stress.

Het eerste deel van de scan (tegel ALGEMEEN) kan de rundveehouder invullen aan zijn bureau. Het gaat hierbij om vragen rond huisvesting, ras en verschillende kengetallen

Daarnaast zijn er de scans voor in de stal zelf. 

Na het invullen van de vragenlijst krijgt de veehouder automatisch via e-mail een rapport teruggestuurd. Daarin staat ook de welzijnsradar (zie figuur). Hierin worden verschillende welzijnsindicatoren weergegeven op een schaal van 0% (zeer slecht) tot 100% (zeer goed). De veehouder krijgt ook online meer informatie rond mogelijke risicofactoren (www.dierenwelzijnscan.be). Hij kan dan overleggen met de bedrijfsdierenarts welke maatregelen mogelijks toegepast kunnen worden om het dierenwelzijn te verbeteren.

Als de scan op regelmatige tijdstippen (bijvoorbeeld tweemaal per jaar) wordt afgenomen, kan ook de evolutie van het dierenwelzijnsniveau op het bedrijf opgevolgd worden. Ook kan het effect van aanpassingen van het management op het dierenwelzijn nagegaan worden.

Bij voldoende deelname kunnen leden van Boerenbond hun score bovendien vergelijken met de scores van collega veehouders. Dit uiteraard wel geheel anoniem.

name: M- tool Drying off selectively - Selectief Droogzetten
title: Selectively drying off dairy, for reduced use of antibiotics
titleOther: Selectief droogzetten van melkvee, voor verminderd antibioticagebruik
desc:
The demand for the reduction of antibiotics in animal husbandry is getting louder and louder. On dairy farms,  drying off selectively is a way to achieve this, provided certain conditions are met.
Selective drying off consists of only drying off infected cows with antibiotics; the non-infected animals are not treated with antibiotics but must be (extra) protected against new udder infections by optimising drying off management (housing, feeding, vaccination...) and inserting an internal teat valve. Selective drying off is an option on well-managed dairy farms with low infection pressure.
A first step is therefore to take a close look at one's own operational management. Monitoring the tank milk cell count over a longer period of time is an aid to evaluate udder health throughout the farm. A tank milk cell count that is too high demands an improvement of the general udder health before applying selective drying off. If good udder health is met, the second step is to determine which cows are infected. This can be done today by means of a recently developed infection indicator. After all, we want to administer long-acting antibiotics to cows with a high risk of infection at the time of drying off, while cows with a low risk of infection can be dryed off without long-acting antibiotics. It is always recommended to protect the cows with an internal teat valve.
With an educational module you can check to what extent your farm is eligible to selectively dry off cows. In addition, based on the MPR data, you can estimate for each individual cow how likely it is that she will be infected with a harmful mastitis agent at the end of lactation. This information helps to make the right drying decision in consultation with the veterinarian supervising the farm.
descOther:
De vraag naar vermindering van antibiotica in de veehouderij wordt steeds luider. Op melkveebedrijven is selectief droogzetten een manier om dit te bekomen, mits voldaan wordt aan enkele voorwaarden.
Selectief droogzetten bestaat erin enkel de geïnfecteerde koeien met langwerkende antibiotica droog te zetten; de niet-geïnfecteerde dieren worden niet met antibiotica behandeld maar dienen (extra) beschermd te worden tegen nieuwe uierinfecties via optimalisatie van het droogstandsmanagement (huisvesting, voeding, vaccinatie…) en het inbrengen van een inwendige speenafsluiter. Op goed geleide melkveebedrijven waar een lage infectiedruk heerst is selectief droogzetten een optie.
Een eerste stap is dus de eigen bedrijfsvoering onder de loep nemen. Het tankmelkcelgetal over een ruimere tijd opvolgen is hierbij een hulpmiddel om de uiergezondheid op het hele bedrijf te evalueren. Een te hoog tankmelkcelgetal vraagt om de algemene uiergezondheid te verbeteren vooraleer selectief droogzetten toe te passen. Indien voldaan wordt aan een goede uiergezondheid, is de tweede stap het bepalen welke koeien geïnfecteerd zijn. Dit kan vandaag door middel van een recent door ons ontwikkelde infectie-indicator. We willen immers langwerkende antibiotica toedienen aan koeien met een grote kans op infectie op het moment van droogzetten, terwijl koeien met een lage kans op infectie zonder langwerkende antibiotica kunnen drooggezet worden. Het is steeds een aanrader de koeien te beschermen met een inwendige speenafsluiter.
Met een educatieve module kan u nagaan in hoeverre uw bedrijf in aanmerking komt om koeien selectief droog te zetten. Daarnaast kan per individuele koe op basis van de MPR-gegevens ingeschat worden hoe groot de kans is dat ze op het einde van de lactatie geïnfecteerd is met een schadelijke mastitisverwekker. Deze informatie helpt om in overleg met de bedrijfsbegeleidende dierenarts de juiste droogzetbeslissing te nemen.

The data exchange platform solves a fundamental problem in the digitalisation of agriculture: It enables farmers and agricultural contractors to exchange data between machinery and agricultural software applications from a wide variety of vendors.

Each user can create a personal agrirouter account and creates their own data stream consisting of his individual machinery and management systems. In the control centre, only they can determine the routes through which his data is transmitted. Deze rekenmachine berekent voor jou op welke manier jij het percentage eiwit van eigen land kan verhogen. Het is ontwikkelt om jou als melkveehouder te ondersteunen bij het zoeken naar mogelijkheden om dit percentage toe te laten nemen op een betaalbare manier.

- voerwinst maximalisatie
- percentage eiwit van eigen land maximalisatie
- melkproductie maximalisatie

Deze doelen worden door andere melkveehouders gezien als de belangrijkste doelen voor een melkveebedrijf. Heb jij andere doelen? Laat het ons weten!

desc:
With Best4Soil we are building a community of practice network across Europe by inter-connecting growers, advisers, educators and researchers. This network promotes knowledge ready for practice on 4 best practices (compost, green manure, anaerobic disinfestation, (bio) solarisation) for the control of soil borne diseases. Therefore we build a website and organize meetings and events in 20 European countries where we exchange knowledge on soil health with our communities of practice. The main objective of the Best4Soil thematic network is to maintain, improve or re-establish soil health in Europe. We provide open-access databases with information on the range of pathogens and nematodes that affect vegetable, arable and cover crops to help practitioners to build appropriate crop rotations and innovative control strategies. 
Innovative control strategies are provided through easily understandable tutorial videos and through factsheets which give more in-depth information. All information is edited in 22 EU languages, will be freely accessible and highly comprehensible to guarantee a smooth knowledge transfer from research to practice.

name: RISE (Response-Inducing Sustainability Evaluation)
title: RISE – getting sustainability down to earth
titleOther: RISE - Nachhaltigkeit be-greifbar machen
desc:
RISE is an indicator- based method for assessing the economic, social and environmental sustainability performance of agricultural production at the farm level. The purpose of RISE is to contribute to enhancing the sustainability of agricultural production, by supporting knowledge-based processes that are founded on voluntary participation, confidentiality and capacity building. RISE users work in agricultural consultancy, education, in development projects and in raw material sourcing. The steps of a RISE analysis are goal and scope definition, farmer selection and contacting, data collection and interpretation, farmer feedback discussion and reporting.
The RISE method was developed at the School of Agricultural, Forest and Food Sciences (HAFL, www.hafl.bfh.ch), a department of the Bern University of Applied Sciences. Since the year 1999, RISE has been used on more than 6000 farms in around 60 countries worldwide. HAFL and its partner institutions offer training courses, RISE analyses of single farms and farm groups, as well as RISE user licenses and technical support.
descOther:
RISE ist eine indikatorbasierte Methode zur ganzheitlichen Analyse der Nachhaltigkeit der landwirtschaftlichen Produktion auf Betriebsebene. Der Zweck von RISE ist, weltweit zur Erhöhung der Nachhaltigkeit der landwirtschaftlichen Erzeugung beizutragen. RISE ist als Baustein wissensintensiver Prozesse konzipiert, die auf Freiwilligkeit, Vertrauen und Kapazitätsaufbau setzen. Anwender der Methode sind Mitarbeiter und Mitarbeiterinnen in der landwirtschaftlichen Beratung, Ausbildung und Entwicklungszusammenarbeit. Schritte des RISE-Prozesses sind Vorbereitung, Datenerhebung, Auswertung, Rückmeldung, Diskussion und Berichterstattung.
Die RISE Methode wurde an der Hochschule für Agrar-, Forst- und Lebensmittelwissenschaften (HAFL, www.hafl.bfh.ch), einem Departement der Berner Fachhochschule, entwickelt. Seit 1999 wurde die RISE-Methode weltweit auf über 6000 Betrieben in 60 Ländern eingesetzt. Die HAFL und ihre Partner bieten Trainingskurse, RISE-Analysen von Einzelbetrieben und Betriebsgruppen sowie RISE-Lizenzen an.

name: Teagasc Short messaging System (SMS) for messaging client farmers and students
title: A SMS system for advisors to keep in touch with clients through mobile/smart phone
desc:
Teagasc Advisory and education services staff have used use a Short Messaging Service (SMS) to send regular targeted text messages to all its clients and students for the last 15 years. With more than 98% of client farmers using mobile phones this technology is fast, cheap, visual, mobile and programmable. Over the last 15 years the usage has grown from 15,000 text messages to over 2 million texts in 2019 to 45,000 clients and 8,000 students.Fast -	Text messages will arrive within minutes of being sent.  Group texts can be sent to multiple members at the same time.
Cheap -	At 4-5c/message these are considerably cheaper than post or voice message.
Visual -	We know that most people learn or remember better from a visual image than from a sound, e.g. seeing 4.00 p.m. Thursday written down will stick in the memory better than hearing it spoken.
Mobile -	For the message sender you can send individual and group texts from anywhere with phone reception. For the receiver, the message will remain on the phone until they decide to delete it.
Programmable - You can when sending texts, programme a set time and date in advance.  

The system is called PUCA www.puca.com and it is relatively old at 15years, it has been very popular with Teagasc staff particularly busy advisers who want to keep regular contact with their clients. This was the preferred system many years ago, it enabled multiple regional, sectoral, and advisor based groupings with the potential to send out SMS messages to as many or as few as required.

Looking at usage, the most common activity is the use of PUCA SMS to remind farmer clients of group meetings, local farm walks and regional/national events. It is also used extensively to remind farmers of critical dates. It has also been useful in giving alerts to farmers relating to weather and disease pressure.   

Advisors have in many cases progressed to using other messaging platforms Whats-app and various social media platforms. These offer a more interactivity and will no doubt continue to expand. Teagasc plan to link SMS to its new CRM system soon. 
During the first few months of this year with Covid 19 restrictions affecting advisory and education activities the SMS system has seen a rapid increase in use as advisors use it to alert farmer clients and students to the challenges faced and the workaround solutions in place.
keywords: Messaging, text, alerts, notifications

title: Advisors record, edit and submit daily farming and rural radio content to Mid West Radio local radio station to be published at a regular time each day.
desc:
Twelve advisors on a 3 week rota, do a circa 4-5 minute pre-prepared monologue on 2-3 current topics each day, on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays. These are broadcast after the 10 pm news on the local radio station Mid West Radio: MWR.
Six advisors also rotate to do a  circa 10-12 minute weekly interview slot with relevant Teagasc staff , farmers or people with something to offer, that is included as a regular insert on a Farming Matters program on Wednesday nights between 10.00 – 11.00 PM.
The rota is set up and manged locally, everyone knows when they’re on: a log is kept on the Teagasc internal document management system to avoid duplication of topics.
The broadcasts are done throughout the year apart from August, Christmas, and Public Holidays, so its 5 days a week most of the year.
There are  4 dedicated desk-top computers, microphones, and basic mixing desks in the 4 regional offices: recordings are made (monologue or interview) on relevant software: it used to be Cool Edit in the past; its Adobe Audition now. This allows us to edit what we do: trim it / bring up volume / add in extra bits etc.
With current Covid 19 restrictions offices are closed phone Apps are being used to do the slots at home: Clear Record, Auphonic, Voice Recorder are the free Apps of choice: downside is that you can’t edit the piece on the phone: in the offices we could record on the phone app, and e-mail it  and edit it on Adobe Audition on the dedicated desktop. Pieces can be e-mailed to MWR and they can do a bit of trimming pauses at the start and end of it if we ask them to. 
Going back a few years when it started some training was given by MWR personnel about how to use the technology, and how to do the programs in terms of delivery / speed / pace / number of topics etc. etc.: how to make it sound good / how to keep listeners engaged etc. New presenters have got some training since: not all of them; some advisors take to it  more easily than others, experienced advisors assist the newer presenters when they start. The co-operation with MWR has been good, we try to deliver MWR listeners require, and both ourselves and MWR want it to sound as professional as possible.

name: PastureBase
title: PastureBase Ireland is the number one tool to help Irish dairy, beef, and sheep farmers manage their grass production and utilisation
desc:
Since 2013, Ireland’s national agricultural research organisation Teagasc, have provided PastureBase Ireland (PBI) as a grassland management system to provide information and advice for Irish farmers. PBI is a grassland management decision support tool and a mechanism to capture background data on farms. PBI stores all grassland measurements in a common structure. It allows the quantification of grass growth and Dry Matter (DM) production (total and seasonal) across different enterprises, grassland management systems, regions, and soil types using a common measurement protocol and methodology. The capture, through the database, of on-farm grassland measurements from research and commercial farms will provide valuable strategic data for the grassland industry. 

PastureBase has 5,000+ users. Among other features, the PastureBase database has weekly records of grass covers for individual farms from 2013 to the present. A grass cover for a farm is principally, the amount of grass available on that farm for cows to eat; formally, it is a measure of biomass in grass on the farm above ground level or a height of 4cm. PBI allows farmers to enter this grass cover data for each field/paddock of their farm in a given week, using their own measurements/estimates, thus allowing them to budget grass-availability for their herd. Additional features are continuously being added to improve the user experience and the quality of the information available to the farmer user. 

Why farmers and advisors use PastureBase?
-PastureBase Ireland farmers grow more grass than the average farmer (NFS)
-Increased grass utilisation equates to more profit for the farmer
-Able to enter data through our smart phone app
-Benchmark against other farms in your discussion group or locality
-An array of tools, grass wedge, rotation planners, budgets, reports

How using PastureBase benefits the farmer and their farm?
-Can quantify the amount of grass on their farm on a given day
-Farmer is able to plan their grazing week ahead
-Easier to communicate to farm employees
-Able to calculate the amount of grass grown on the farm
-Increase output – livestock are grazing high quality grass throughout the grazing season
-Able to use supplementation strategy – reduce input costs

PastureBase is easy to use:
-A smartphone app is available
-The app works offline
-Export data to PDF and excel, so you can save or email results to others
-One app can manage multiple farms

name: Kialo
title: Kialo (kialo.com) is a public discussion platform designed to facilitate reasoned debates about complex topics online.
desc:
Kialo describes itself as “a debate platform powered by reason” to encourage clear and concise arguments from both sides.  It is a public discussion platform designed to facilitate reasoned and civilised debates about complex topics online. It launched in 2017 and has grown into a community with thousands of debates and millions of contributions. Kialo is a purpose-built tool for critical thinking, thoughtful discussion, and collaborative decision-making. It works far better than meetings and lengthy email chains, or debates on social media platforms. Discussions are presented in structured argument “trees” that allow others to understand quickly why a decision was made, and who was swayed which way.

Users find themselves confronted by a series of opinionated statements; i.e. such as “Digital technology will reform agriculture” which is accompanied by an image. These are the site’s theses or the issues users can debate. Each thesis takes a particular stance on a topic, thus inviting users to respond with claims that support the stance or disagree with it by inputting pros and/or cons to the statement. There is a ranking system for contributors to vote on claims and counterclaims, but the aim is to judge their impact on the claim, not on their amusement or outrage.

By clicking on a thesis or its accompanying image users are taken to a page that shows the full thesis and a circular infographic. These infographics are one of Kialo’s proprietary design features: dual-colored visual representations of what the site calls the “discussion typology.” Each discussion automatically tracks and collates certain information about the discussion. A coloured circle with linear stalks radiating from it in all directions represents the evolution of a discussion. Kialo is particularly useful for advisors during Covid-19 to facilitate group work with clients.
keywords: Discussion, communication, group

Advisor Prime is Trimble’s intelligent, fully integrated web-based solution featuring streamlined workflows for creating and sharing management zones and variable rate prescriptions. By using Advisor Prime, you’ll reduce data entry errors created by repetitive field-by-field procedures, cut out hours of processing time, and eliminate steps in transferring data back to the farmer.

Precision Zone Management — Advisor Prime’s robust zone management tool reduces the time and effort required to detect patterns in multiple data layers, including crop health imagery, EC data, elevation maps, or yield data. Use your own style and agronomic principles to:

• Select number of zones
• Set zone sizes
• Edit zones
You can then apply these settings to multiple clients, saving time and reducing headaches.

Mobile Soil Sampling — Advisor Prime comes with with the Trimble® Ag Mobile app, available for both Apple iOS and Android devices. When it comes to soil sampling, no other app makes the process easier. Create grids on the fly or display background zones for each field. See where you logged the actual point and send all data back to your computer without worrying about USB sticks or cables. With our mobile app you can:

• Create any grid size
• Load background zone maps
• Navigate to target points
• Complete work without an internet connection

Soil Lab Compatibility — Advisor Prime users can work with any soil lab and take advantage of our streamlined process to import soil test results for your clients. Further, you can easily print bag labels and lab submission sheets by field or in bulk. Advisor Prime makes it easy to manage the soil analysis process and create prescriptions from the resulting data.

Variable Rate Prescriptions — How much time do you spend creating fertility and seeding prescriptions and sharing them with farmers? This manual process can result in many painstaking hours and unexpected errors — right in the middle of your busiest time of year. With Advisor Prime, you can define when formulas are used and how fertilizer applications will be calculated, to make both initial prescriptions and last-minute changes quick and easy.

The best part? Your variable rate prescriptions can be easily shared with customers, especially if they use Farmer Pro. Once permission is granted, connect with your customers’ Farmer Pro accounts and quickly share prescriptions without a USB drive. Advisor Prime supports a wide range of controllers to drive field applications. No other software solution is easier to use.

Clean Yield Data — Are you tired of looking at yield maps that don’t match what’s in the field? Trimble Ag Software’s new Yield Data Cleaning tool automatically fixes issues with grain flow delays, GPS errors, sensor errors, and overlaps — saving you countless hours manually fixing them field-by-field. As more and more farmers move toward precision ag, accurate yield maps become critical when using them for prescriptions or management zones. Clean yield data means accurate maps, which result in more profitable acres.

Crop Scouting — Advisor Prime includes the ability to leverage the Trimble Ag Mobile app for crop scouting. The best part? Multiple users can enter crop scouting records at the same time, sending data back to one central location. Advisors can quickly analyze the results and create recommendations in a timely manner.

With our mobile app you can:

name: Teagasc Biomass Calculator
title: Teagasc has developed an Excel Calculator which calculates the net cash flow over a 20 year investment period in willow and miscanthus.
desc:
Crops such as willow and miscanthus have a role to play in providing energy as well as reducing greenhouse gas emissions. However, these crops are difficult to evaluate economically compared with more conventional farming enterprises. For instance, willow is planted only once and is harvested only every two or three years in a 20-year plus cycle. Furthermore, willow is an expensive crop to establish. A breakdown of operational and materials costs involved in the establishment of a biomass crops is therefore extremely important. There are numerous assumptions which can be made. Teagasc has developed a spread sheet which can determine the annual net cash flow based on such assumptions which include the following variables:
- Bank interest rate
- General inflation rate
- Energy inflation rate
- Not VAT registered
- Initial establishment costs borrowed over 20 years
- No willow or miscanthus gate fee for sludge
- No carbon premium
- 50% of the establishment costs covered by grant aid
- Annual Land Opportunity Cost (OC)/ha

 The spreadsheet can be accessed by a farmer through their local advisor.

In a livestock building, the air is charged with water vapor, gas, microorganisms and dust. To maintain a healthy atmosphere and preserve the health of animals, it is important to eliminate these elements by regularly renewing the air in the building. Quality air will also be beneficial for the health of those who work there and for the sustainability of livestock facilities and equipment.
Using the wind to renew the air in buildings means benefiting from a free resource! To get the most out of it, you have to think carefully about the orientation and design of the buildings.

Stemming from the collaboration between IDELE and the company Eternit, the objective of Shelt-air is to correctly size the ventilating openings (in long pan and in ridge) and to choose well its materials of cladding, according the type and number of animals housed, the environment of the building more or less exposed to the wind and the volume of the building.
